name: The Cramps
label: Vengeance
lede: A rockabilly record collection, a Memphis studio and a mental-hospital gig: the Cramps built psychobilly out of nothing, then left an album in a garage for decades.

eras.title: A hitchhiker, a record collector, and no bass
eras.text: Erick Purkhiser and Kristy Wallace met on the side of a road, drove to Ohio, then to New York, and showed up at CBGB with a rockabilly collection and no interest in playing bass. The lineup they settled on had two guitars and a drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lux Interior · Wikipedia: Poison Ivy (musician) · Vice: The Guide to Getting into The Cramps · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: A hitchhiker gets picked up outside Sacramento
years.p: Erick Purkhiser and a friend pull over for Kristy Wallace. Wikipedia dates it to 1972; Vice calls them Sacramento State students who shared a mania for obscure singles, horror comics and early sci-fi.
years.xp:
Purkhiser took the name Lux Interior from an old car commercial. Wallace, who says hers came to her in a dream, started as Poison Ivy Rorschach, after the inkblot test's inventor. They moved to Ohio and then, in 1975, to New York, where the downtown scene at CBGB and Max's Kansas City included the Ramones, Patti Smith, Television and Blondie.

Ivy and Lux stayed married until his death in 2009, 37 years by Wikipedia's count.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bryan Gregory · Wikipedia: The Cramps · Vice: The Guide to Getting into The Cramps
years.h: Two guitars, no bass, and Bryan Gregory's sister on drums
years.p: The Cramps' first line-up is Lux Interior, Poison Ivy Rorschach, guitarist Bryan Gregory and his sister Pam Balam.
years.xp: Gregory, born Gregory Beckerleg in Detroit, met Lux while working at a New York record store. His striped black-and-white hair and oozing guitar sound made him half of the band's look. Ivy has said the band coined 'psychobilly' in 1976, adding that all the 1950s rockabillies were psycho to begin with. Vice traces the word to a Johnny Cash song from the same year.

years.h: Miriam Linna takes over the drums for the debut
years.p: Linna is behind the kit for the band's debut on November 1, 1976, and stays until July 10, 1977.
years.xp: Linna went on to found the Brooklyn label Norton Records in 1986 and run it for decades. She and her husband Billy Miller also formed the A-Bones, and Bob Dylan recommended her drumming on his radio show in 2007, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Memphis tapes, a mental ward
eras.text: A drummer swap, an Alex Chilton session in Memphis and a free show for the patients of a California state hospital. By the end of 1978 the band had two singles out and a piece of video that people still trade.

years.h: Nick Knox, ex-Electric Eels, takes the drum stool
years.p: Knox replaces Linna in September 1977 and outlasts every other Cramps drummer, staying until 1991.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Knox with bringing a tightness to the band's sound. His cousin Mike Metoff would later fill in on guitar for a European tour, and Knox died in 2018.

years.cap: The Cramps live in Lokeren, Belgium, 2006 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Alex Chilton · Wikipedia: Gravest Hits · The Big Takeover: The Cramps - Gravest Gravy (Vengeance Records)
years.h: Alex Chilton produces the Cramps at Ardent in Memphis
years.p: The October 1977 sessions with Big Star's Alex Chilton feed the first singles, the first EP and, decades later, a whole album nobody had heard.
years.xp: Chilton met the band around CBGB. The Ardent tapes produced the 1978 singles 'Surfin' Bird' and 'Human Fly' and the Gravest Hits EP. The rest sat in reels until 2026, when they became Gravest Gravy.

years.h: 'Surfin' Bird' and 'Human Fly' come out on Vengeance
years.p: The band's first two singles, both produced by Chilton, appear on their own Vengeance imprint.
years.xp: Both sides of the two singles would be collected on the 1979 Gravest Hits EP. 'Human Fly' has since turned up in UK television and, in a cover by Hanni El Khatib, in a Nissan ad, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Target Video filmed the show at Napa State Hospital.
q: Somebody told me you people are crazy, but I'm not so sure about that.
years.src: Washington Post: Lux Interior, 62 · Wikipedia: Target Video
years.h: A free show for the patients of Napa State Hospital
years.p: The Cramps and the Mutants play for an audience of mostly mental patients, about 100 people, and Target Video films it.
years.xp:
The footage became Live at Napa State Mental Hospital. Lux told the crowd what he'd heard about them, per the Washington Post obituary, and then declared he wasn't so sure it was true.

Wikipedia says Rolling Stone later called the show a landmark moment for punk rock.

eras.title: Records, a lawsuit, and a vanished guitarist
eras.text: The first EP and the first LP, both made with Chilton, arrive. Then Bryan Gregory quits, the band moves to Los Angeles, and a dispute with I.R.S. Records ends up in court.

years.h: Gravest Hits, five songs on a 12-inch
years.p: Illegal and I.R.S. issue the EP: both sides of the Vengeance singles plus 'Lonesome Town'.
years.xp: The back sleeve is a live shot from CBGB's 2nd Avenue Theatre in New York. The liner notes thank 'Dr. J.H. Sasfy, Professor of Rockology' of the American Rock'n'Roll Institute in Washington, D.C.

years.src: Wikipedia: Songs the Lord Taught Us · Vice: The Guide to Getting into The Cramps
years.h: Songs the Lord Taught Us, cut in Sam Phillips's studio
years.p: The debut LP is recorded at Phillips Recording in Memphis, produced by Alex Chilton with engineer John Hampton. 'Garbageman' is the lead single.
years.xp: The album came out on I.R.S. in the US and Illegal in the UK. Wikipedia lists Pitchfork at 8.7 and notes Rolling Stone put it on its 2020 list of the 80 greatest albums of 1980.

years.h: Bryan Gregory walks out in 1980
years.p: The striped-haired guitarist quits abruptly. He later plays in Beast and shows up as a zombie in George Romero's Day of the Dead.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Gregory married the Australian producer Robyn Hunt in Cleveland in 1984, and that his look made regular work hard. He ended up managing an adult bookstore.

years.big: A name off a Santería candle
years.h: Kid Congo Powers leaves the Gun Club for the Cramps
years.p: Lux picks 'Kid Congo' from the label copy on a Santería candle, and the band keeps 'Brian' out of it to stay clear of Gregory.
years.xp: Kid Congo Powers, born Brian Tristan, left the [[Gun Club|e78cc47f-9b89-4ef7-86f8-8f9df4f9dac9]], which he had started with [[Jeffrey Lee Pierce|83107f93-2d1a-474b-8f73-1147c13391cb]], before its debut album. He later joined [[Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds|172e1f1a-504d-4488-b053-6344ba63e6d0]] from 1986 to 1990 and now leads the Pink Monkey Birds.

years.h: Psychedelic Jungle: half covers, all Cramps
years.p: Cut in January 1981 at A&M Studios in Hollywood, self-produced, with seven originals and seven covers.
years.xp: Kid Congo and Nick Knox play on it; Donna Santisi shot the front cover and Anton Corbijn the back. Wikipedia notes 'Goo Goo Muck' streams jumped 9,500 percent after it turned up in Netflix's Wednesday.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Cramps · Wikipedia: Bad Music for Bad People
years.h: The Cramps and Miles Copeland end up in court
years.p: Wikipedia says a dispute over royalties and creative rights with I.R.S. head Miles Copeland went to litigation and kept new records off shelves until 1983.
years.xp: The 1984 compilation Bad Music for Bad People was the label's answer.

eras.title: Live tape, borrowed guitar
eras.text: With the lawsuit in the way, the band goes live and goes to Europe. The lineup is down to a duo, a drummer and whoever they can get.

years.src: Wikipedia: Smell of Female · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: Smell of Female recorded live at the Peppermint Lounge
years.p: Six songs on a mini-album, cut over two nights at the New York club. It reaches No. 74 in the UK.
years.xp: It came out on Big Beat in the UK, Enigma in the US and New Rose in France. New Rose also issued a four-7-inch box set. Kid Congo left after it, Wikipedia says.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Cramps · Wikipedia: Nick Knox
years.h: Nick Knox's cousin Ike plays guitar for a European tour
years.p: Mike Metoff of the Pagans covers after Kid Congo's exit. The tour had been canceled twice for lack of a guitarist, and it sells out four nights at London's Hammersmith Palais.
years.xp: The band also taped an appearance for A Midsummer Night's Tube, playing 'Thee Most Exalted Potentate of Love' and 'You Got Good Taste'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bad Music for Bad People
years.h: I.R.S. compiles Bad Music for Bad People
years.p: Eleven songs from 1977 to 1979 on a label the band is fighting. Wikipedia calls it a cash-grab in fans' eyes.
years.xp: Sounds gave it five stars while criticizing the release, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Ivy plays bass on 'Surfin' Dead' for a zombie movie
years.p: For The Return of the Living Dead, Ivy plays both bass and guitar on the song, the band's first move towards a bass sound.

eras.title: Bass guitar, Elvis, and a UK hit
eras.text: The band adds bass for good, makes its biggest record in Europe, and finally gets a Top 40 single. Then the drummer and bassist both leave.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Date with Elvis (The Cramps album) · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: A Date with Elvis is the Cramps' biggest record in Europe
years.p: Recorded at Ocean Way in fall 1985 and issued on Big Beat, it reaches No. 34 in the UK. The US gets it in 1990.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it sold over 250,000 copies in Europe. Ivy sings lead on 'Kizmiaz', the only album where she does. Robert Palmer of the New York Times called it the band's best: 'the Cramps have learned to focus and intensify'.

The tour ran six nights at Hammersmith, three at the Odeon and three at the Palais, each opening with the members walking on one at a time to 'Heartbreak Hotel'.
play: Can Your Pussy Do the Dog?

years.h: Candy Del Mar, ex-Satan's Cheerleaders, becomes permanent bassist
years.p: Jennifer 'Fur' Dixon toured the album first; Del Mar makes her recorded debut on the live RockinnReelininAucklandNewZealandxxx.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stay Sick! · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: Stay Sick! gives them a UK Top 40 single
years.p: 'Bikini Girls with Machine Guns' reaches No. 35, the band's only UK Top 40 hit, with Ivy posing as the girl with the gun.
years.xp: Poison Ivy produced it at Music Grinder in Hollywood. The title comes from a saying of Ghoulardi, Cleveland's horror host. It was the last studio album with Knox.

years.src: Wikipedia: Look Mom No Head! · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: Look Mom No Head! arrives with a new rhythm section
years.p: Nick Knox and Candy Del Mar are gone. Slim Chance plays bass and Jim Sclavunos drums; Iggy Pop guests on 'Miniskirt Blues'.

eras.title: Warner money, Beverly Hills, SpongeBob
eras.text: A major-label imprint, network TV and a run of records that keep the trash-and-Elvis template intact. Then it ends on a stage in Arizona.

years.h: The Medicine Label signs them, and Conan books them
years.p: Warner's imprint announces the deal with a 500-copy live 12-inch handed to ticket holders at a secret CBGB show. Harry Drumdini, who joined in 1993, plays drums.
years.xp: The record captured the band's first two Max's Kansas City shows. The Cramps made their US network debut on Late Night with Conan O'Brien, playing 'Ultra Twist'.

years.h: Flamejob is cut in Earle Mankey's Psychedelic Shack
years.p: Released in the UK on Creation, with Slim Chance on bass and Drumdini on drums; Lux took the cover photo.

years.h: They play the Beverly Hills, 90210 Halloween episode
years.p: In 'Gypsies, Cramps and Fleas' they perform 'Mean Machine' and 'Strange Love'.
years.xp: Lux opens the set with: 'Hey boys and ghouls, are you ready to raise the dead?'

years.h: Big Beat from Badsville is all originals
years.p: Recorded at Earle Mankey's house in May 1997 and released on Epitaph, it is the only Cramps album with no covers.
years.xp: NME gave it 3 out of 10, per Wikipedia. The Cramps reissued it in 2001 on their own Vengeance label with four bonus tracks including 'Peter Gunn'.

years.h: Bryan Gregory dies at 49
years.p: Wikipedia says he drove himself to the emergency room feeling run down and died of heart failure at Anaheim Memorial Medical Center.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lux Interior · Wikipedia: The Cramps
years.h: Lux voices a cartoon rock singer on SpongeBob
years.p: He plays the lead singer of the Bird Brains in 'Party Pooper Pants', singing 'Underwater Sun'.

years.h: Fiends of Dope Island, the last studio album
years.p: Recorded in Hollywood in August 2002 and released on Vengeance, the Cramps' own label, with Chopper Franklin on bass.

years.cap: The last show was in Tempe.
years.h: The last show: Marquee Theatre, Tempe, Arizona
years.p: The Cramps play their final gig on November 4, 2006, after summer dates in Europe.

eras.title: Ivy keeps the tapes
eras.text: Lux Interior dies. His widow keeps the archive, and in 2026 two Washington punk lifers help her open it.

years.src: Washington Post: Lux Interior, 62 · NPR: Cramps Frontman Lux Interior Dies At 62 · Wikipedia: Lux Interior
years.h: Lux Interior dies at 62
years.p: The Washington Post and NPR reported a heart ailment; Wikipedia cites aortic dissection at Glendale Memorial Hospital.
years.xp: A memorial was held on February 21 at the Windmill Chapel of the Self-Realization Fellowship Lake Shrine, per Wikipedia. The band split. The Washington Post noted that a drum head he put his head through is held by the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

years.h: Nick Knox dies at 65
years.p: Wikipedia gives cardiogenic shock as the cause.

q: I've never been more excited about a record and I'm not even on it!
years.src: Mother Jones: How Two Punk Icons Are Giving the Cramps a Second Life · Paste: Ian MacKaye and Henry Rollins to revive The Cramps' formerly defunct label
years.h: Two punk lifers, a cargo van and a garage of tapes
years.p: Henry Rollins drives the Cramps' tape archive from Los Angeles to Nashville on his own dime. Ian MacKaye is in on it, too.
years.xp: Ivy's tapes had been sitting in her Los Angeles garage, and Mother Jones reported signs of moisture. Rollins and MacKaye are reviving Vengeance with Larry Hardy of In the Red and Jimmy Maslon. 'Of course Ian and I are going to work for free', Rollins told the magazine.

years.src: The Big Takeover: The Cramps - Gravest Gravy (Vengeance Records) · Stereogum: Ian MacKaye & Henry Rollins Releasing Shelved 1977 Cramps Album · Metacritic: Gravest Gravy by The Cramps
years.h: Gravest Gravy, a 1977 album finally released
years.p: The Vengeance set holds the shelved Ardent sessions produced by Alex Chilton. Pitchfork rated it 8.6.
years.xp:
Stereogum's tracklist has 11 songs, including 'Weekend on Mars', 'Jungle Hop' and 'Twist & Shout'. The Big Takeover says Brian Kehew transferred the tapes, Rollins curated, Ian MacKaye and Don Zientara engineered at Inner Ear and Pete Lyman mastered. Rollins says the cover art is by Stephanie Chernikowski.

Metacritic lists a Metascore of 90 from eight reviews, and its summary of Pitchfork's 86 says it's like being 'brained with a flying chair'.
